title: Floating Promise in Security Handlers
platform_conditions: Promise semantics of the JavaScript runtime apply wherever the compiled JavaScript runs (Node.js server handlers, browsers)
security_mechanism: verifyPermissions(req) without await starts the check and returns a Promise the handler discards; the next() call runs immediately, so the request is dispatched while the authorization is still pending -- and when the check later resolves or rejects, nothing consumes the result. A rejected permission check becomes an unhandled rejection (crash or log line) while the request already completed. The type signature reveals the bug (Promise<void> discarded) but tsc does not error without lint enforcement, so the hole ships silently.

source_sink_clues.source: Async authentication/authorization/rate-limit functions invoked in middleware and handlers whose Promise is not awaited.
source_sink_clues.sink: Discarded Promise results before security decisions and sensitive operations in middleware chains

tracking_guards: Check every security-decision call in middleware is awaited before next(); check the codebase enforces no-floating-promises (eslint rule) in CI; check rejections in these handlers fail closed by short-circuiting the response.
not_candidate_when: The operation is deliberately parallel with a later await/Promise.all before the guarded branch, the function is synchronous, or the middleware awaits inside a wrapper that propagates rejection into the response path.
synthetic_safe_example: app.use(async (req, res, next) => { await verifyPermissions(req); next(); });
public_references: CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html
TypeScript Handbook: tsc CLI options (strict family) — https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/compiler-options.html
